video.title: Find and fix bugs: Be a bug detective
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds. Code is typed out on a card, left to right in both languages. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Mr Joseph — the students’ computer studies teacher (main character)
Ms Salma Haddad — the students’ maths teacher (cameo)
Narrator — the Darsi voice, talking to the student (warm, peer to peer)

scenes.narration: My robot was supposed to reach the target. It walked into the wall instead! Something in my program was wrong.
Today: bugs, and how to find and fix them.
A mistake in a program is called a bug. Every programmer makes bugs, even the best ones. Finding and fixing them is called debugging. It’s like being a detective.
First, run the program and watch carefully. Where does the robot go? Point to the first card where it goes the wrong way.
Then change just that one card. Don’t change everything! Run it again and see if it works. If not, find the next wrong card.
A detective doesn’t guess. She looks for clues, one at a time. You do the same: watch, find the clue, fix, and check again.
Quick check! The robot should go forward, turn right, forward. My cards say forward, turn left, forward. Which card is the bug?
The turn! It should be turn right. Change only that card, run it again, and the robot reaches the target.
Programmers often write the cards as words, one on each line. This is the same program, written as code. Each line is one card. Can you read it?
In the app, open Program a robot and try grids five and six. When the robot bumps, find the first wrong card and fix only that one.
Your turn. Your robot bumps into a wall. What do you do first?
Find the first wrong card. Remember: a bug is a mistake, and everyone makes them. Test, find the first wrong step, change one thing, and test again.
Try it yourself: hide a bug. Draw a robot path on paper, write the cards, and put one wrong card in. Can a friend or someone at home find your bug?

checkpoints.prompt: Wanted: forward, turn right, forward. Cards: forward, turn left, forward. Which card is the bug?
checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — it turns left instead of right. Change only that card.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — compare card by card: the turn goes the wrong way.

checkpoints.prompt: Your robot bumps into a wall. What do you do first?
checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — find the first wrong card, change it, and test again.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — don’t start again. Find the first wrong card and change only that.
